newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish settlers lay claim to West Bank hilltop.
newsitem.headline: Jewish settlers lay claim to West Bank hilltop.

text.p: Jewish settlers laid the cornerstone of a new settlement in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday in response to the killing of a settler and her 12-year-old son by Arab gunmen last week.

"We decided in their memory to go up the hill...and establish a new neighbourhood of Beit El," Hagi Ben-Artzi, settler activist and brother-in-law of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, told Reuters.
Beit El residents Etta Tzur and her son Ephraim were killed by Palestinian guerrillas in a drive-by attack near self-ruled Ramallah last week.
"We always welcome, especially after this murder, an infusion of life," settler leader Aharon Domb told Israel Radio.

Netanyahu's government, which has approved the building of thousands of West Bank homes since taking power in June but has not allowed new settlements to be built, has not approved construction at the site.

The Palestinian Ministry of Information held the Israeli government responsible for the settlers' action, blasting Netanyahu for trying to "destroy the peace process and push the area to the brink of explosion and war."

Israel's Peace Now group, which virulently opposes Jewish settlements in lands Israel seized in the 1967 Middle East war, warned Netanyahu and Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai that "a new settlement is bound to cause a new eruption."
Netanyahu's office and the Defence Ministry declined comment on the incident.

The right-wing Israeli government has come under growing international criticism since it overturned a four-year freeze on settlement construction shortly after ousting Israel's previous centre-left government in May election.

U.S. President Bill Clinton on Monday embraced the tough language of his predecessor George Bush on the settlement issue. Asked at the White House if he would call settlements an obstacle to peace, he told reporters: "Absolutely".

Some 130,000 Jews have settled among more than two million Arabs in the West Bank and Gaza -- where Palestinians hope to establish an independent state -- since Israel seized the areas in the 1967 Middle East war.
Settlers, whose support helped Netanyahu to an upset victory in May, have complained the new government has done little to make good on promises to bolster new settlement construction.
Said settler leader Domb of the Netanyahu government: "We have quarrels, but they are lover's quarrels."
